text: The subtype is exactly probability measures satisfying `HasFiniteMoment p`: [Villani, Definition 6.3 in the linked draft](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82) defines the classical finite-p carrier this way. The [integral comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L705) turns `MemLp` into finiteness of ∫d(x,y)^p on an ordinary Borel metric space. At p=∞, [Mathlib’s actual Lp conventions](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92) instead requires essentially bounded distance. The carrier itself permits other exponents; every metric constructor explicitly requires p≥1. The [Dirac-component equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L319) preserves the underlying law. An arbitrary anchor is identified with this space only when it has finite moment, as [the exact anchor criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L822) requires.
For a finite nonzero exponent and finite measure, compares MemLp moment with the actual integral about a prescribed basepoint.
Identifies the carrier with finite distance from the Dirac law, including the infinite exponent.

`∃ x, MemLp (fun y ↦ edist x y) p ν` means that distance from some basepoint is a.e. strongly measurable and has finite Lp seminorm. For finite nonzero p, [the published integral equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L705) agrees with [Villani, Definition 6.3 in the linked draft](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82). [Basepoint independence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L698) correctly assumes an ordinary pseudometric, a finite measure, and measurability of the new distance section. Extended-space comparisons require finite distance between basepoints. At p=∞ the predicate expresses essential boundedness; p=0 retains [Mathlib’s actual Lp conventions](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92) and is not used to assert a metric. No basepoint is chosen by this existential definition.
For a finite nonzero exponent and finite measure, compares MemLp moment with the actual integral about a prescribed basepoint.
A concrete Dirac measure has finite moment at every exponent.
Checks basepoint independence under the actual measurability and finite-measure hypotheses.

The subtype condition is precisely Wp(μ₀,μ)<∞, matching [the Layer 3 specification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L507). It constrains displacement, not moment. With measurable ground distance, [self-distance is zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L392). The [anchor criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L822) identifies this carrier with Pp exactly when μ₀ has finite moment. The concrete Cauchy check passes: a finite second moment would imply an integrable identity, contradicting [the Cauchy(0,1) theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Cauchy/Basic.lean#L250), although that law lies in its own component. This uses the published L²⊆L¹ interfaces, not a new standalone fixture. The raw carrier permits all p; metric constructors require p≥1.
Checks the exact finite-moment hypothesis on a general anchor; no unconditional equality of the two carriers is asserted.
On the real line, finite second moment implies MemLp id at exponent2. Composed with finite-measure L²⊆L¹, this is the first step of the concrete Cauchy exclusion.

At location0 and scale1, the actual Cauchy law has nonintegrable identity. Together with finite-moment L² membership and L²⊆L¹ this excludes P₂; this theorem alone is not called a Wasserstein-membership fixture.

`⟨μ,hμ⟩` packages the supplied probability law with its proof of finite moment, exactly the constructor promised by the docstring. The [projection equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L290) returns μ, and [the reverse equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L308) reconstructs every space element. These checks exclude replacing the law by a default or a chosen representative. Different proofs of the same property give the same element by subtype extensionality. No p≥1 hypothesis is needed merely to construct this carrier; it is imposed by the metric instances.
Checks that construction preserves the supplied probability law exactly.
Checks reconstruction from the underlying law and its membership proof.

The constructor packages μ with the actual condition Wp(μ₀,μ)≠∞. Its argument is finiteness of displacement from the fixed anchor, not finite moment of μ. The [projection formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L139) returns the original law; [reconstruction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L158) is the reverse identity. Thus it implements [the documented component](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L77) without changing measures or assuming the anchor has finite moment. Proof irrelevance removes dependence on the supplied finiteness proof, including at the endpoint p=∞.
Checks that construction preserves the supplied probability law exactly.
Checks reconstruction from the underlying law and its membership proof.

`μ.1` forgets only the finite-moment proof, returning the same bundled probability measure. The [constructor formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L290) and [injectivity theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L269) verify both the value and absence of identifications between different laws. This matches [the subtype definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L88). The map does not choose a pointwise density or an optimal coupling. The induced measurable structure is inherited from probability measures; equality with the Borel structure of the Wasserstein metric is a separate theorem.
Checks that forgetting the membership proof does not identify distinct probability laws.

The first projection returns exactly the probability measure in the anchored subtype. [Evaluation after construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L139) is μ, and [injectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L115) proves that no distinct laws are collapsed. Only the proof of finite Wp distance from the anchor is forgotten. This is precisely the forgetful map of [the component definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L77), valid for all exponents and extended ground distances. It does not claim the law has finite moment or introduce a second measurable structure.
Checks that forgetting the membership proof does not identify distinct probability laws.

The conclusion is the second field of [the defining subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L88): the underlying probability law has the same exponent-p moment property used to admit it. The two coercions only forget the subtype and probability-measure wrappers. [Reconstruction with this proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L308) returns the original element. This assertion is independent of a chosen basepoint and does not strengthen an existential moment condition to every basepoint on an extended metric space.

The theorem projects precisely the finiteness proof in [the component subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L77). Its anchor, exponent and underlying law are unchanged, so the prose “finite Wasserstein distance from μ₀” agrees exactly with `≠ ⊤` in ENNReal. [Reconstruction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L158) verifies that this property and the underlying law recover the element. No claim of a finite moment follows for an arbitrary anchor; [the separate anchor criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L822) supplies that distinction.

The constructor uses Wp of the underlying laws as `edist`, with the actual zero, symmetry and triangle proofs. [The triangle theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L602) requires standard-Borel structure, measurable ground distance and p≥1; the signature retains all three. Thus it implements [the Layer 3 specification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L507) on extended pseudometric bases, including p=∞, without assuming separation. Finiteness within the component is established separately by [the anchor-triangle argument](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L201). The published two-Dirac and pseudometric controls check the distance convention; no completeness or finite-support density claim is bundled here.
Computes the exact two-Dirac distance as ground edist for every nonzero exponent.
Checks zero-distance points in a pseudometric base. Their Borel Dirac laws are equal; this is not an example of distinct laws at zero distance.

The [proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L201) uses Wp(μ,ν)≤Wp(μ,μ₀)+Wp(μ₀,ν). Symmetry turns the first term into the finite quantity stored in μ; ν supplies finiteness of the second. ENNReal addition preserves finiteness, so `edist μ ν ≠ ⊤` is exactly the advertised conclusion. The standard-Borel, measurable-distance and p≥1 assumptions support this triangle argument. No finite moment of the anchor is needed, and the reasoning also covers p=∞.

The instance converts the component’s extended pseudometric to an ordinary pseudometric using [proved finiteness of every pairwise distance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L201). Consequently taking `toReal` cannot collapse an infinite distance to zero. The [distance formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L220) confirms dist(μ,ν)=Wp(μ,ν).toReal, as required by [the Layer 3 specification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L507). The p≥1 assumption is retained. Separation is not asserted on a general pseudometric ground space, and finite moment of an arbitrary anchor is unnecessary.
Checks the installed real distance equals the real value of Wp.

The instance upgrades the actual Wp pseudometric by separation of probability laws. The [uniform separation theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L1220) splits finite nonzero p from p=∞; in the latter case W₁≤W∞ reduces zero-distance separation to W₁. The signature retains complete, second-countable Borel metric hypotheses and p≥1. [The real-distance formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L478) and pairwise finiteness ensure `dist=0` means Wp=0. The two-Dirac check recovers the ground distance. This establishes a metric only: completeness of the Wasserstein space and its Borel compatibility remain separate results.
Computes the exact two-Dirac distance as ground edist for every nonzero exponent.
Checks finite-exponent separation using equality of actual measures on a Polish metric base.
Checks separation at the infinite exponent separately.

Both directions leave the underlying probability measure unchanged. Their membership proofs use [the exact Dirac identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L744): finite moment iff Wp(δx₀,μ)<∞. The ordinary pseudometric and Borel hypotheses justify changing from the existential basepoint to x₀. [The two coercion identities](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L331) verify the maps explicitly, including p=∞; p=0 is only a carrier equivalence under the stated Lp convention. No arbitrary anchor is substituted for δx₀. The finite-p case agrees with [Villani, Definition 6.3 in the linked draft](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82); the essential-supremum endpoint is supported by [Mathlib’s actual Lp conventions](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92).
Checks that the forward Dirac-component identification leaves the law unchanged.
Checks that its inverse also leaves the law unchanged.

`PseudoEMetricSpace.ofEDist` installs Wp on the finite-moment subtype and supplies zero, symmetry and triangle with their actual hypotheses. In particular, p≥1, standard-Borel structure and joint measurability are explicit; the ground space here has an ordinary pseudometric. This is [the Layer 3 specification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L507) for Pp(X). [Pairwise finiteness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L404) follows from the finite-moment coupling criterion, while [the evaluation theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L465) confirms the installed distance. Separation and completeness are additional properties, not assumptions hidden in this constructor.
Checks that the installed extended distance is exactly Wp of the underlying laws.
Checks zero-distance points in a pseudometric base. Their Borel Dirac laws are equal; this is not an example of distinct laws at zero distance.

This instance takes the real value of the installed Wp extended distance only after [proving it finite for every pair of finite-moment laws](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L404). The [distance identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L478) therefore has the intended value, with no infinite-to-zero fallback. The p≥1 and measurable standard-Borel hypotheses supporting the pseudometric laws are retained. [The Dirac-component equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L319) checks that this finite-moment carrier agrees with the conventional anchored construction. At p=∞ the same reasoning gives a pseudometric but makes no claim that its topology is the finite-p topology.
Checks the installed real distance equals the real value of Wp.

The [Lean conclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Lie/Ado/ArbitraryField.lean#L113) is an injective Lie homomorphism into Endₖ(V) for some finite-dimensional K-module V: exactly a faithful finite-dimensional representation, as in [Barnes, introduction](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/34B6179FF194E4DD2A18B7F69E1F902A/S1446788700008600a.pdf/adoiwasawa_extras.pdf#page=1). The only hypotheses are a field, the Lie structures and finite dimensionality; neither algebraic closure nor a characteristic bound is hidden.

The previous missing [Checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/AdoIwasawa/README.md#L519) now pass. Explicit instantiations on gl₂(𝔽₂) and gl₂(𝔽₃), including the characteristic-two strengthened branch, compile against the cached 715 build; all Lie-representation sources are unchanged at d96. `#print axioms` reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, agreeing with the current d96 extractor audit. These are diagnostic instantiations, not newly published example theorems. No fresh d96 rebuild is claimed.

Published positive-characteristic branch has no prime-size restriction. A diagnostic instantiation on gl₂(F₂) compiles in cached715; its source is byte-identical at d96 and current extracted axioms are standard-only. This is not a claim of a new published F₂ example.
The actual basis/coordinate construction equates finite-dimensional faithful representations with injective maps into matrix Lie algebras, preserving the intended meaning of faithfulness.

[Lean](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Generation/HilleYosida/Generation.lean#L197) matches [Engel–Nagel II.3.8](https://www.math.uni-tuebingen.de/de/forschung/agfa/members/engel-nagel_one-parameter-semigroups.pdf): dense real Banach-space domain, every positive resolvent power bounded by M/(λ−ω)ⁿ, and a semigroup with growth M exp(ωt) whose generator equals A including its domain. Actual resolvent membership supplies closedness; a separate premise is unnecessary.

The [acceptance examples](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemigroups/README.md#L158) pass by composing published facts: [multiplication generator −m and resolvent](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Multiplication/Basic.lean#L124), [bounded exponential generator](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/BoundedGenerator/Basic.lean#L141), [Neumann series](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/BoundedGenerator/Resolvent.lean#L70), [resolvent identities](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Resolvent/Identity.lean#L211) and [contraction bound](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Resolvent/Basic.lean#L395). The last bound applies to nonnegative multiplication; arbitrary bounded A instead has 1/(λ−‖A‖). These are direct specializations through proved comparison maps, not newly named fixtures. The exact compositions compile at715; all involved semigroup sources are unchanged atd96. No fresh d96 build is claimed.
The published multiplication semigroup has the actual generator −m as a partial linear map, with full domain.
For m ≥ 0, identifies the actual contraction-semigroup resolvent with multiplication by (lambda + m)⁻¹. Composing this equality with the published norm theorem checks the concrete operator bound.
The actual exponential semigroup e^(tA) has generator A on the full Banach space.
The actual bounded-exponential resolvent equals its convergent Neumann series for lambda > norm A.
Identifies the semigroup integral resolvent with the actual Banach-algebra inverse (lambda − A)⁻¹; enables the concrete identity and bound without an assumed comparison.
Specialized at the already published ofMultiplication m hm constructor, gives the concrete resolvent identity with sign mu − lambda.
Specialized at ofMultiplication m hm and rewritten by its published resolvent equality, gives the concrete multiplier bound 1/lambda.
Specialized at ofBounded A and rewritten by the published resolvent bridge, gives the actual inverse resolvent identity.
Specialized at ofBounded A and its growth bound gives 1/(lambda − norm A); 1/lambda is the contraction specialization, not a bound for arbitrary bounded A.

[Lean](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Generation/LumerPhillips.lean#L96) matches [Engel–Nagel II.3.14–3.15](https://www.math.uni-tuebingen.de/de/forschung/agfa/members/engel-nagel_one-parameter-semigroups.pdf): dense domain plus norm dissipativity and surjectivity of λI−A at one positive λ characterize contraction generators. Surjectivity makes A closed, so generator equality is with A itself, including its domain. No Hilbert-space hypothesis is needed.

Specialized at ofBounded A and rewritten by the published resolvent bridge, gives the actual inverse resolvent identity.
Specialized at ofBounded A and its growth bound gives 1/(lambda − norm A); 1/lambda is the contraction specialization, not a bound for arbitrary bounded A.
